title: Route Flyover Preview: Fly Your Route First
description: Preview a route from the air with the Route Flyover Preview — the camera tilts to 60 degrees and flies the routed path before you drive it. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, thirty seconds of flyover shows what the leg table cannot: the valley the road threads, the ridge it climbs, and the town it threads between two lakes.
quick_answer: The Route Flyover Preview tilts the map to 60 degrees and flies a camera along the routed path, turning with the road, so you feel the journey's shape. Add start, stops and destination, start flyover, and stop it when you have seen enough — or ride it to the finish.

body.t: A leg table says 212 miles and 3 h 39 min. The flyover says: an hour of plain, a pass, then the lake road. Both are the same route; the second is the one the passengers remember being promised.
The camera turning with the road exposes the junction maze the directions mumble through — noticed here, briefed before the drive, survived calmly during it.

faq: Is this a rendered video?
No — it is the live map tilted to 60° with the camera animated along the routed path. Nothing is pre-rendered or downloaded as a film.
Can I stop it?
Any time — stop mid-flight and the map is yours again; or let it run and it levels off at the finish.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. The flyover flies the route's geometry, not this hour's congestion.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
The camera follows the road's own line, windings included — the flyover's length is the journey's real shape.
Can route results change over time?
The route beneath can change as road data improves; the flight is generated fresh from today's route each time.
Does it show terrain and scenery?
It shows the map's own rendering tilted — roads, water, towns and the shape of the land as the map draws them. It is a preview of shape, not a photograph.
Can I fly a cycling or walking route?
Fly the route any of the site's planners builds — the camera is indifferent to the wheels beneath it.
Can I fly just one leg?
Build the route with fewer stops and the flight shortens to the leg you care about.
Does it need a fast connection?
It streams the live map as it flies, so a reasonable connection keeps the flight smooth.
Can passengers watch it offline?
The flyover is live-map based; the roadbook is the offline companion. Fly it at home, print the book for the car.
